chunks: She said: 'O nobles, advise me in this matter. I do not decide any thing until you concur.'

key_terms.أَفْتُونِي: advise me, give me your opinion
key_terms.أَمْرِي: my matter, the issue at hand
key_terms.الْمَلَأُ: the nobles, the council of leaders

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about consultation and decision-making in leadership?
ai.summary: In this verse, Queen Bilqis demonstrates the Islamic principle of *shura* (consultation) by seeking the consensus of her nobles before finalizing her decision, a practice highly valued in Shia political thought for legitimate governance. Her phrase 'until you have given your counsel' underscores the necessity of collective deliberation among experts, reflecting the structured hierarchy of authority in the Sabaean kingdom. This narrative serves as a model for leaders to balance executive authority with the wisdom of their advisors.
